title: She coined a term 40 million people have since used to examine their own minds
sources: American Bazaar, July 1, 2026 - Four Indian Americans make Carnegie's 2026 Great Immigrants list
caption:
In 1995, she coined a term that changed how psychology understands prejudice. In 2026, the US named her one of its Great Immigrants for it.

Mahzarin Banaji, born in Secunderabad, was named to Carnegie Corporation's 2026 Great Immigrants, Great Americans list. In 1995, she and Anthony Greenwald defined 'implicit bias' - automatic, unintentional associations people don't consciously realize they hold - and in 1998 co-developed the Implicit Association Test to measure it. The test has since been taken by over 40 million people worldwide, on race, gender, class and more. She's now the Richard Clarke Cabot Professor of Social Ethics at Harvard.

A word she invented in a lab is now a word millions use to examine themselves - that's not just an academic career, that's a permanent shift in how people think.
